title: Shared Counts Across Two Permutation Prefixes
statement:
You get two arrays a and b of length n. Each one is a permutation of the numbers 1 to n.

Return an array shared of length n where shared[i] is how many numbers appear both in a[0..i] and in b[0..i] (the first i + 1 elements of each).

examples.why: After one step the prefixes are {2} and {3}: nothing shared. After two, both are {2, 3}. After three, {1, 2, 3} and {2, 3, 4} share 2 and 3.
2 sits at the same index in both, but 1 and 3 only meet once both prefixes are complete.
Identical arrays share every number as soon as it appears.

constraints: a and b are permutations of 1..n
hints: Going from step i − 1 to step i, only two numbers enter the prefixes: a[i] and b[i]. Can the answer change because of anything else?
A number becomes shared at the moment its second appearance happens, whichever array that is in.
Keep a count of how many times you have seen each number. When a count reaches 2, the shared total goes up by one. Remember that a[i] and b[i] may be the same number.

explain.intuition:
Each number appears exactly once in each array. So a number is shared from the step where it has been seen twice in total, once in each prefix, and never stops being shared. You do not need to compare whole prefixes; just watch for second sightings.

Keep seen[x], the number of times x has shown up so far. At step i, bump seen[a[i]] and seen[b[i]]. Every bump that lands on 2 adds one to a running total. If a[i] == b[i], the second bump is the one that reaches 2, so it is counted correctly once.
steps: Create seen of size n + 1 filled with 0, and total = 0.
For each i: increment seen[a[i]]; if it is now 2, increment total.
Increment seen[b[i]]; if it is now 2, increment total.
pitfalls: Counting only positions where a[i] == b[i]. Shared numbers can sit at different indexes.
Adding 2 when a[i] == b[i] because both bumps "see" the number. Only the bump that reaches exactly 2 counts.
Recomputing a set intersection for every prefix, which is O(n²).

solutions.title: Intersect the prefixes at every step
solutions.idea: For each i, put a[0..i] into a set and count how many of b[0..i] are in it.

solutions.title: Count second sightings
solutions.idea: A number becomes shared when it has been seen twice. Track counts and a running total.

followups: The arrays are no longer permutations and may contain repeats. What does "shared" mean now, and how do you count it?
With n ≤ 50, the two inputs fit into 64-bit masks. How would you compute each answer with a single AND and a popcount?
lcTitle: Find the Prefix Common Array of Two Arrays
